correctness.rationale: The torus-fixed pairs are precisely diagram inclusions of size difference two avoiding cell (u,v). A complete three-case classification of two-box skew diagrams gives t2=binom(d,2)+h+b. Splitting a diagram across column u, conjugating the overhang and isolating the unique boundary-horizontal-domino event produces the displayed finite rational formula for all u,v>=1. Pole-order calculation yields the asymptotic. A standard-library exact checker independently enumerates pairs for all 16 u,v<=4 and 14 colengths, checks deletion statistics for all partitions of sizes 2..18, the closed (2,2) series and symmetry. The finite tests do not replace the general combinatorial proof.

originality.rationale: The claimed invariant counts two-step incidences of distinct ideals, not singleton Hilbert schemes, generator-refined single ideals, or one-box nested flags. Current source comparisons found no stronger statement covering all multiplicities and all lengths. An exact witness on x^2 y^2 distinguishes the two-step count from the prior one-step statistic: partitions (4) and (2,2) have equal one-box extension counts but respectively 4 and 5 two-box extension counts. Historical priority is provisional, particularly for older reduced-node flag literature.

value.rationale: The two-step nested punctual Hilbert scheme is a natural incidence moduli problem, not recoverable just by counting the smaller and larger single ideals or their one-box extensions. The proof gives one rational all-length Euler series uniformly for arbitrary independent fat-node multiplicities, explicit nonreduced (2,2) data and a sharp polynomial-growth asymptotic. The boundary correction measures an essential interaction between overhang and bounded partition tails.
